title: Data drill: Crumb & Co
intro: Read the case study first. Then choose which calculations are worth doing, work them out, and decide what the numbers show and where you would use them.
caseHtml:
Crumb & Co Ltd

Crumb & Co Ltd runs three bakeries in Reading. It is known for its sourdough bread and its celebration cakes, which customers order online for birthdays and weddings.

In March 2025 Crumb & Co raised the price of a sourdough loaf. The owner, Hannah Price, is thinking about raising it again in 2026, and wants to grow sales of celebration cakes.

Table 1: Sourdough loaves
Before March 2025After March 2025
Price per loaf£3.20£3.60
Loaves sold per week4,0003,700

Average incomes in Reading rose by 3% in 2025. Over the same period, orders for celebration cakes rose by 7.5%.

questions.text: Analyse one way in which the price elasticity of demand for sourdough might affect Crumb & Co’s decision to raise its price again.
Assess whether Crumb & Co should rely on celebration cakes to grow its revenue.
Crumb & Co wants to increase its revenue. Evaluate two ways it could do this and recommend which is most suitable.

calcs.why: Worth doing. This is the key figure for Question 1 and supports a price rise as one option in Question 3.
calcs.formula: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price

meaning.q: What does a PED of -0.6 tell Hannah?
opts: Demand is price inelastic, so a price rise is likely to increase revenue from sourdough
Demand is price elastic, so she should cut the price
Price changes have no effect on sales
meaning.why: Quantity changes by a smaller percentage than price, so revenue rises when price rises. This may not hold if the price keeps going up.

use.why: This is the key figure for Question 1 and supports a price rise as one option in Question 3.

calcs.t: Change in weekly revenue from sourdough
calcs.why: Worth doing. Shows the effect of the last price rise, which is useful evidence for the next one.
calcs.formula: Revenue = price × quantity; new revenue − old revenue

opts: The price rise increased revenue, but Crumb & Co sells 300 fewer loaves a week
meaning.why: Revenue went up even though volume fell. Profit probably rose by more than £520, because 300 fewer loaves means lower costs.

use.why: Shows the effect of the last price rise, which is useful evidence for the next one.

calcs.why: Worth doing. Central to whether relying on cakes is wise.
calcs.formula: % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in income

meaning.q: What does a YED of +2.5 mean for Crumb & Co?
opts: Cake sales are very sensitive to income, so they would rise fast when incomes grow but could fall sharply in a downturn
Cake sales do not depend on income
meaning.why: A YED above +1 means demand changes by more than income. Good when incomes rise, risky when they fall.

use.why: Central to whether relying on cakes is wise.

calcs.t: Crumb & Co's share of town-centre bakery sales
calcs.why: Worth doing. Supports an argument about how much power Crumb & Co has over price.
calcs.formula: Sales of the business ÷ total sales in the market × 100

opts: Crumb & Co is a major bakery in the town centre, which may help it raise prices without losing many customers
Crumb & Co is a small player
meaning.why: A quarter of the market is a strong position, which supports the inelastic PED. Customers still have other bakeries to choose from.

use.why: Supports an argument about how much power Crumb & Co has over price.

calcs.why: Crumb & Co is a private limited company. Its shares are not traded on a stock exchange, so there is no share price to use.
There is no share price or dividend information, and Crumb & Co is not a plc.
